title: Perimeters and Areas of Plane Figures
summary: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10,000 cm²; 1 hectare = 10,000 m². Perimeter is a length (cm, m) and area is in square units (cm², m²).

Rectangle: perimeter 2(l + b), area l × b. Square of side a: perimeter 4a, area a² (and area = ½ × diagonal²). Parallelogram: area = base × corresponding height. Triangle: area = ½ × base × height. Right triangle: ½ × product of the legs. Equilateral triangle of side a: height (√3/2)a, area (√3/4)a². Rhombus: area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ (product of diagonals), perimeter 4 × side. Trapezium: area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × distance between them.

For a triangle with sides a, b, c and semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c)/2: area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)]. Example: 13, 14, 15 cm ⇒ s = 21, area = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √7056 = 84 cm². If the sides are in a ratio, find them first from the perimeter: 3 : 5 : 7 with perimeter 60 cm gives 12, 20, 28 cm.

Path round (or inside) a rectangle: area = outer rectangle − inner rectangle (path width w adds 2w to each dimension outside, subtracts 2w inside). Two cross paths of width w through the middle of an l × b park: area = lw + bw − w² (the central square is counted twice). Cost = area × rate.

Circumference = 2πr = πd (diameter = 2 × radius); area = πr². Take π = 22/7 or 3.14 as told. Semicircle (closed): perimeter = πr + 2r, area = ½πr². Ring (circular path) between radii R and r: area = π(R² − r²) = π(R + r)(R − r).

A sector of radius r and central angle θ: arc length l = (θ/360°) × 2πr; area = (θ/360°) × πr² = ½ × l × r; perimeter = 2r + l. A clock's minute hand turns 6° a minute (360° in 60 minutes) and the hour hand 0.5° a minute (30° an hour), so in 20 minutes the minute hand sweeps a 120° sector.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (i) The hour hand of a clock turns through ____ in 30 minutes. (ii) The area swept by a 10 cm minute hand in 20 minutes is ____.

(i) The hour hand turns 30° per hour, so 15° in 30 minutes.
(ii) 20 minutes = 120° = ⅓ of a turn: ⅓ × 22/7 × 10² = 2200/21 ≈ 104.76 cm².
Fill in the blanks: (i) The area of a parallelogram of area 18 cm² on a base of 6 cm has height ____. (ii) The area of an isosceles triangle with base 12 cm and equal sides 10 cm is ____.

(i) Height = area ÷ base = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 cm.
(ii) Height = √(10² − 6²) = 8 cm; area = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 cm².
Write True or False: (i) The area of a sector of radius 6 cm with arc 11 cm is 33 cm². (ii) The circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm is 22 cm.

(i) True: area = ½ × l × r = ½ × 11 × 6 = 33 cm².
(ii) False: 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 cm.
Fill in the blanks: (i) A rectangle with sides in the ratio 5 : 2 and perimeter 98 cm has area ____. (ii) The area of a triangle with base 7 cm and height 6 cm is ____.

(i) 2(5k + 2k) = 98 ⇒ k = 7; sides 35 and 14; area = 490 cm².
(ii) ½ × 7 × 6 = 21 cm².

la: A square of side 4 cm is inscribed in a circle. Find the area enclosed between the circle and the square. (π = 22/7)

The diagonal of the square is a diameter: d = 4√2 cm, so r = 2√2 cm and r² = 8.
Area of circle = 22/7 × 8 = 176/7 ≈ 25.14 cm².
Area of square = 16 cm².
Required area = 25.14 − 16 = 9.14 cm².

A horse is tied with a 14 m rope at one corner of a rectangular field 40 m × 30 m. Find (i) the area it can graze (ii) the area it cannot graze (iii) the increase in grazing area if the rope were 21 m.

The corner angle is 90°, so the horse grazes a quarter circle.
(i) ¼ × 22/7 × 14² = ¼ × 616 = 154 m².
(ii) Field = 40 × 30 = 1200 m²; not grazed = 1200 − 154 = 1046 m².
(iii) With 21 m: ¼ × 22/7 × 441 = 346.5 m²; increase = 346.5 − 154 = 192.5 m².
Find the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 25 cm and 10 cm and whose non-parallel sides are 14 cm and 13 cm.

Draw a line from one end of the shorter side parallel to the non-parallel side of 14 cm. It cuts off a triangle with sides 14, 13 and 25 − 10 = 15 cm.
s = (14 + 13 + 15)/2 = 21; area of triangle = √[21 × 7 × 8 × 6] = √7056 = 84 cm².
Height of the triangle (= height of the trapezium) on base 15: ½ × 15 × h = 84 ⇒ h = 11.2 cm.
Area of trapezium = ½ × (25 + 10) × 11.2 = 196 cm².
